candidate: Codex PreToolUse command hook (Codex CLI 0.167.0)
what: Lifecycle hook that runs a command before shell, apply_patch, MCP and other local tool calls; JSON on stdin, JSON on stdout or exit code 2 to deny. Same wire contract as the hook the kit already uses.
problem_here: Lets the existing guard block killing or overwriting live runs, reading sealed test data and editing the evaluator on Codex, with an adapter instead of a rewrite.
mechanism: Entry under PreToolUse in <repo>/.codex/hooks.json with a match-all matcher; the script prints hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision=deny with a reason, or exits 2 with the reason on stderr; exit 0 with empty stdout allows.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks (vendor docs, read 2026-11-10); https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.167.0/codex-rs/hooks/src/events/pre_tool_use.rs and the generated schemas in codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated (source read 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11). No independent measurement; not exercised locally.
maturity: Ships in Codex CLI (openai/codex, Apache-2.0, about 134.8k GitHub stars on 2026-11-10); hooks are on by default in stable 0.167.0 (2026-11-06); first release of hooks not checked (a third-party guard documents support from CLI 0.125.0).
cost: Adapter for tool names, patch-text parsing and project-root discovery. Fails open on crash, timeout (default 600 s), bad JSON or any exit code other than 2. No ask decision. Needs project trust plus per-hook trust. Does not see hosted web search or input typed into an already running command. Windows quoting is fragile.
simpler_alternative: Rules written only in AGENTS.md (advice, no enforcement).
reason: It is the only per-call deny point Codex offers and it matches the existing guard contract; its weaknesses are documented and can be compensated by rules, sandbox and a liveness check.
cheap_local_trial: In a scratch Git repo add .codex/hooks.json with a PreToolUse hook that denies any command containing a marker word, trust the project and the hook, then run codex exec --sandbox workspace-write with a prompt that asks for that command; expect a blocked call. Repeat on native Windows and in WSL2. Needs a signed-in CLI and a few thousand tokens.

candidate: Guard liveness interlock (hook-issued ticket that the run controller requires)
what: The guard hook leaves a fresh, command-bound ticket each time it lets a protected run-controller command through; the run controller refuses launch, stop and final evaluation when called by an agent without a matching fresh ticket.
problem_here: Codex hooks fail open and are skipped when untrusted or mis-quoted, sometimes while reporting success. Without proof that the guard ran, every guard protection can vanish silently.
mechanism: The hook process (not sandboxed) writes a ticket holding a hash of the command and a timestamp into a kit folder that sandboxed commands cannot write (.codex). The controller recomputes the hash from its own arguments and requires a ticket a few seconds old at most; otherwise it refuses and tells the user to trust the hooks.
evidence: Problem: fail-open branches read in https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.167.0/codex-rs/hooks/src/events/pre_tool_use.rs (2026-11-10); vendor wording that hooks are a guardrail and not a complete enforcement boundary at https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks (2026-11-10); silent non-execution on Windows in https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/38168 (user report, open). The remedy is this scout's proposal and has not been measured by anyone.
maturity: New practice; no existing implementation found; no license question.
cost: About 100 lines of standard-library code. Must tell agent calls from a person typing in a terminal, tolerate concurrent hooks and shell wrappers, and handle clock or path differences. A forged ticket is prevented only while agent commands stay sandboxed.
simpler_alternative: A self-test at session start that only warns when hooks are inactive.
reason: Turns fail-open into fail-closed for the few operations that matter most without depending on undocumented Codex behaviour; needs a pilot because it assumes the hook runs outside the sandbox and can write where agent commands cannot.
cheap_local_trial: Offline: pipe a Codex-shaped payload to the guard in a unit test, then call the controller with and without the ticket. Live: leave the hook untrusted in a scratch repo and confirm the controller refuses to launch.

candidate: Map every guard ask to deny on Codex
what: On Codex the guard never returns the ask decision: each case becomes deny with a reason that tells the agent to hand the action to the user.
problem_here: Codex treats permissionDecision ask as a failed hook and continues the tool call, so an unported guard would silently allow exactly the actions it meant to question.
mechanism: A platform switch in the guard output step; interactive confirmation, where wanted, moves to execution-policy prompt rules.
evidence: Verbatim vendor statement that ask is parsed but not supported and the tool call continues, https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks (2026-11-10); same behaviour in https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.167.0/codex-rs/hooks/src/events/pre_tool_use.rs (2026-11-10). Not exercised locally.
maturity: Behaviour of stable Codex CLI 0.167.0 (2026-11-06); the docs say not supported yet, so it may change.
cost: Stricter than the current behaviour in attended sessions: actions a person could have approved are refused. The guard's fail-safe path (unreadable config turns every action into ask) becomes deny-all on Codex.
simpler_alternative: none found
reason: Required for correctness; the kit already does the same under bypass mode on its current platform.
cheap_local_trial: Unit test: feed the guard Codex-shaped payloads for each ask case and assert the output never contains ask.

candidate: Codex SessionStart hook for live run status
what: Hook that runs at session start, resume, clear, fork and after compaction; plain text on stdout is added to the model's developer context.
problem_here: Ports the kit's session-status injection so the agent knows which runs are live after a restart or compaction.
mechanism: SessionStart entry in <repo>/.codex/hooks.json with matcher startup|resume|clear|compact that runs the existing status script; the docs example also sets an additionalContextLimit value.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks (vendor docs, 2026-11-10): plain stdout becomes extra developer context; sources startup, resume, clear, compact, fork. Not exercised locally.
maturity: Part of Codex CLI hooks (Apache-2.0); stable 0.167.0 (2026-11-06); first release not checked.
cost: Runs on every start; needs project and hook trust; a mis-quoted command on Windows can fail without any visible error (user report https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/57050).
simpler_alternative: One line in AGENTS.md telling the agent to run the status command first.
reason: Direct mechanical equivalent of an existing kit feature at near-zero cost; keep the AGENTS.md line as the fallback when hooks are not trusted.
cheap_local_trial: Scratch repo with a SessionStart hook that prints a marker line; start one codex exec run and ask the model to repeat the marker.

candidate: Codex PermissionRequest hook
what: Hook that runs only when Codex is about to ask the user for approval; it can allow or deny, and any deny wins.
problem_here: Could auto-deny escalation requests that touch protected paths in attended sessions; none found for unattended runs, where no approval request is raised.
mechanism: hookSpecificOutput.decision.behavior set to allow or deny with a message.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks (vendor docs, 2026-11-10). That it does not fire under approval policy never is inferred, not tested.
maturity: Part of Codex CLI hooks; stable 0.167.0; first release not checked.
cost: A second decision point to keep consistent with the pre-tool guard; an allow answer would be a way to approve without a person, which the brief forbids.
simpler_alternative: Deny in the PreToolUse hook, which runs earlier and in every mode.
reason: Adds little over the pre-tool guard; only worth it if attended Codex sessions show approval prompts for protected actions.
cheap_local_trial: Interactive session with on-request approvals and a PermissionRequest hook that denies a marker command.

candidate: Codex Stop hook as loop driver
what: A Stop hook can return decision block with a reason, which makes Codex continue the turn with that reason as a new prompt.
problem_here: Could keep an unattended research loop going inside one session.
mechanism: Stop hook checks loop state and blocks stopping until the budget is spent.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks (vendor docs, 2026-11-10). No measurement of long loops driven this way was found.
maturity: Part of Codex CLI hooks; stable 0.167.0.
cost: Loop control would live inside the agent session: context grows without bound, a failed hook ends the loop silently (fail-open), and budget checks depend on the hook running.
simpler_alternative: Harness code that starts one bounded codex exec per iteration.
reason: The brief wants harness code and a frozen evaluator to decide; an outer process is simpler to bound and to audit.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Codex PostToolUse hook for an execution audit trail
what: Hook after a tool call; it can add feedback or replace the tool result but cannot undo the action.
problem_here: Could record what actually ran, as evidence for reviewers; the kit's guard log records only pre-call decisions.
mechanism: PostToolUse entry appending tool name, command and exit status to a log written by the hook process.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks (vendor docs, 2026-11-10). Not exercised.
maturity: Part of Codex CLI hooks; stable 0.167.0.
cost: Another process per tool call (noticeable on Windows, where a user measured about 230 ms per PowerShell-launched hook, https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49716); duplicates the session transcript that Codex already stores.
simpler_alternative: Read the stored session transcript or the exec JSON stream.
reason: The JSON event stream and the transcript already carry executed commands; no gap shown.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Codex execution-policy rules: forbidden prefixes (.codex/rules/*.rules)
what: Starlark prefix rules evaluated inside Codex before a command runs; decision forbidden blocks without prompting.
problem_here: A second layer for a few fixed-prefix mistakes (force push, killing all Python processes, deleting the runs folder) that still works when the guard hook fails to start.
mechanism: prefix_rule(pattern=[...], decision='forbidden', justification=...) in <repo>/.codex/rules/nn-training.rules, with inline match and not_match examples that Codex validates at load.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/rules (vendor docs, marked experimental, 2026-11-10); https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.167.0/codex-rs/core/src/exec_policy.rs (2026-11-11). Not exercised.
maturity: Part of Codex CLI; docs label rules experimental; stable 0.167.0 (2026-11-06) added a managed prompt-user decision, so the area is still moving.
cost: Prefix matching only. Shell scripts with redirection, variables, substitution or control flow are not split, so inner commands escape the rule. Needs a trusted project. codex exec --ignore-rules skips it. Behaviour on a rules syntax error was not checked.
simpler_alternative: Rely on the guard hook alone.
reason: Cheap defence in depth that does not share the hook's fail-open weakness; trial first because the API is experimental and matching is easy to dodge.
cheap_local_trial: Offline, no session and no tokens: codex execpolicy check --pretty --rules <file> -- git push --force, and the same for a compound shell line to see what does not match.

candidate: Codex execution-policy rules: prompt prefixes as the port of ask rules
what: Prefix rules with decision prompt ask the user before a matching command runs.
problem_here: Ports the kit's ask rules (for example before git push) to attended Codex sessions, where the hook cannot ask.
mechanism: prefix_rule(pattern=['git','push'], decision='prompt', justification=...). With approval policy never, which is the codex exec default, the same rule becomes forbidden with the reason: approval required by policy, but AskForApproval is set to Never.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/rules (2026-11-10); constant and match arm read verbatim in https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.167.0/codex-rs/core/src/exec_policy.rs (2026-11-11). Not exercised.
maturity: Part of Codex CLI; rules are labelled experimental; stable 0.167.0.
cost: Same matching limits as forbidden rules. Unattended, the agent sees a refusal and may look for another route; the guard must cover variants.
simpler_alternative: Deny in the guard hook in all modes.
reason: Gives ask in attended use and deny in unattended use, which is the behaviour the kit already documents for its current platform.
cheap_local_trial: codex execpolicy check against the rule offline; then one interactive session and one codex exec run asking for git push in a scratch repo with no remote.

candidate: Codex execution-policy allow rule that runs the training launcher outside the sandbox
what: A prefix rule with decision allow makes Codex run the matching command without prompting and outside the sandbox.
problem_here: GPU device nodes are reported missing inside the Linux and WSL2 sandbox, and the recommended Windows sandbox stops leftover child processes. The launcher needs a narrow exit without switching the whole session to full access.
mechanism: prefix_rule allowing only the launcher prefix (interpreter, controller path, launch). Codex skips the sandbox only when every parsed command segment matches an explicit allow rule.
evidence: Vendor docs describe allow as running outside the sandbox without prompting, https://developers.openai.com/codex/rules (2026-11-10); source comment read verbatim in https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.167.0/codex-rs/core/src/exec_policy.rs (2026-11-11). GPU problem: user reports https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/19676 and https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/57042 (open, no fix recorded). Combination not exercised.
maturity: Part of Codex CLI; rules experimental; stable 0.167.0.
cost: A hole by design: whatever follows the launcher prefix runs unsandboxed with network and can read sealed data, so the guard and the launcher must validate the training command. Prefix matching is brittle across interpreter spellings and absolute paths; a compound command loses the match and falls back into the sandbox.
simpler_alternative: Run the whole session with danger-full-access inside a container, or have the person start training by hand.
reason: Probably the narrowest way to train on a GPU from an unattended Codex run without bypassing approvals, but every link is untested here.
cheap_local_trial: In WSL2: allow rule for a one-line script that prints whether CUDA is available; run it through codex exec --sandbox workspace-write with and without the rule and compare. Repeat on native Windows with a child process that should outlive the command.

candidate: Codex permission profiles (beta) with deny entries for sealed test data
what: Named profiles in config.toml that set per-path read, write or deny for sandboxed commands, enforced by the operating-system sandbox.
problem_here: OS-level block on reading the held-out test set from agent commands, stronger than pattern matching in the guard.
mechanism: default_permissions = 'nn-training'; [permissions.nn-training] extends = ':workspace'; under filesystem ':workspace_roots' the sealed globs are set to deny.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/permissions (vendor docs, marked beta, 2026-11-10). Not exercised; no independent test found.
maturity: Beta in Codex CLI; /permissions profile selection and presets arrived in 0.164.0 (2026-10-23) per the changelog.
cost: Ignored when sandbox_mode is set anywhere or --sandbox is passed. Deny globs are expanded when each process starts. Not enforced by the Windows unelevated sandbox. Does not cover commands that an allow rule runs outside the sandbox, which includes training itself. Needs trusted project config or user config, written as TOML.
simpler_alternative: Keep the test split outside the repository, as the kit's README already advises.
reason: The only OS-enforced read block available, but beta and with sharp interactions; offer it as a hardening option after a local test.
cheap_local_trial: codex sandbox --permission-profile <name> -- a command that prints a sealed file, in a scratch repo; expect a denial. No model session needed.

candidate: Unattended baseline: codex exec --sandbox workspace-write with approval policy never and network off
what: Headless run in which edits are confined to the workspace, nothing can prompt, and commands have no network.
problem_here: Gives the unattended mode a starting permission set that needs no approval bypass.
mechanism: codex exec defaults to a read-only sandbox and approval policy never; --sandbox workspace-write widens writes to the working directory and temp folders; .git, .agents and .codex stay read-only; network stays off unless configured.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/noninteractive and https://developers.openai.com/codex/agent-approvals-security (vendor docs, 2026-11-10); default approval policy read verbatim in https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.167.0/codex-rs/exec/src/lib.rs (2026-11-11); flags confirmed in local help of codex-cli 0.167.0-alpha.3.2.
maturity: Stable Codex CLI 0.167.0 (2026-11-06). The --full-auto shortcut was removed, so flags do change.
cost: No GPU inside the Linux and WSL2 sandbox (user reports), no Git writes, package installs fail without network, and a refused action is returned to the model, which may try workarounds. Sandbox escapes were reported and fixed in 2026, so it is a strong default rather than a guarantee.
simpler_alternative: Read-only sandbox (cannot edit code, so no research loop).
reason: Narrowest documented setting in which an agent can still change code; satisfies the brief's rule against bypassing approvals.
cheap_local_trial: In a scratch Git repo: codex exec --sandbox workspace-write --json with a prompt that writes one file inside and one outside the repo; expect the second to fail.

candidate: Codex automatic approval review (--approve-for-me, approvals_reviewer = auto_review)
what: A reviewer model answers approval requests in place of a person, with on-request approvals and the workspace-write sandbox.
problem_here: Would let an unattended run get sandbox escalations approved with nobody present.
mechanism: Each approval request goes to a reviewer model; reviewer failures and timeouts deny the action.
evidence: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands?surface=cli and https://developers.openai.com/codex/agent-approvals-security (vendor docs, 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11); local help text. No published accuracy figures were found.
maturity: Present in stable 0.167.0; changed in each of 0.165.0, 0.166.0 and 0.167.0 per the changelog.
cost: Approval becomes a model judgement that a prompt injection could sway; extra model calls per request; conflicts with --sandbox; behaviour changed in three consecutive releases.
simpler_alternative: Approval policy never plus explicit rules, so every decision is deterministic.
reason: The brief wants decisions from measurements the agent cannot influence; a model-granted approval is not that, and no evidence of its reliability was found.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox (alias --yolo)
what: Runs every command without sandbox and without approvals.
problem_here: Makes GPU access and background processes work at once; it is what a popular auto-research skill for Codex uses by default.
mechanism: Single flag on codex or codex exec; it also skips the Git-repository check.
evidence: Local help of codex-cli 0.167.0-alpha.3.2; its help text reads: EXTREMELY DANGEROUS. Intended solely for running in environments that are externally sandboxed (re-read 2026-11-11); a third-party skill starts this way, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leo-lilinxiao/codex-autoresearch/main/README.md (2026-11-11).
maturity: Stable flag in Codex CLI.
cost: Removes every Codex-side protection; only the fail-open hook remains. Directly against the brief unless inside an isolated container.
simpler_alternative: workspace-write plus a narrow allow rule for the launcher.
reason: Forbidden by the brief outside an isolated container; document it only as part of the container mode.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust for headless runs
what: Runs enabled hooks without requiring stored hook trust, for one invocation.
problem_here: Hook trust is stored in the user's home configuration and the CLI has no command to grant it; without trust the kit's guard is skipped. The flag makes a headless launcher run the guard anyway.
mechanism: Flag on codex and codex exec, passed to the session as bypass_hook_trust; disabled hooks stay off.
evidence: Local help text (intended only for automation that already vets hook sources); https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.167.0/codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/discovery.rs (2026-11-11). Not exercised.
maturity: Present in codex-cli 0.167.0-alpha.3.2; first release not checked.
cost: Trust is bypassed for every enabled hook in every layer, including hooks that a repository change or a plugin added, so the launcher must first check that the only declared project hooks are the kit's and that their files match known hashes.
simpler_alternative: One interactive visit to /hooks per machine, repeated whenever a hook declaration changes.
reason: Better than running unguarded, but it widens trust beyond the kit; acceptable only behind a launcher-side integrity check, and the interactive route should stay the default.
cheap_local_trial: Scratch repo with an untrusted hook that writes a marker file; run codex exec with and without the flag and look for the file.

candidate: Per-invocation project trust through a -c override
what: Passing the project trust entry on the command line so the project .codex layer (hooks, rules, config) loads without editing the home configuration.
problem_here: The installer must not touch the home directory, yet an untrusted project silently loses the guard hook and the rules.
mechanism: codex exec -c with the key projects.'<absolute path>'.trust_level set to trusted. The loader merges command-line overrides before it decides project trust.
evidence: Merge order read verbatim in https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.167.0/codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs (2026-11-11). Not documented by the vendor and not exercised.
maturity: Undocumented behaviour of 0.167.0; may change without notice.
cost: Relies on an implementation detail; path spelling on Windows may matter; a launcher that grants trust on the user's behalf must only do so after an explicit opt-in.
simpler_alternative: Ask the user to trust the project once in the interactive prompt.
reason: Could remove the main first-run obstacle for headless use without writing to the home directory, if it works.
cheap_local_trial: Scratch repo never opened in Codex, with a hook that writes a marker file: run codex exec with the override and the hook-trust bypass flag and check for the marker.

candidate: Agent Skill at .agents/skills/nn-training (SKILL.md with references and scripts)
what: Codex loads skills from .agents/skills in the project and from the home directory; SKILL.md needs name and description, and may ship scripts and references.
problem_here: Carries the kit's operating procedure and on-demand references to Codex in the same format the kit already uses.
mechanism: Copy the skill folder to <repo>/.agents/skills/nn-training; Codex lists it by description and loads it implicitly or when the user types the skill name after a dollar sign.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills (vendor docs, 2026-11-10). A source study of eleven coding agents found SKILL.md skills in nine of them, https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00006 (v1, 15 Jul 2026, abstract only, read 2026-11-11). Not exercised locally.
maturity: Stable in Codex CLI 0.167.0; first release not checked; the vendor catalog openai/skills has about 28.7k stars.
cost: Paths inside the skill text differ from the current copy. The skills list is capped at 2 percent of the context window, so a long description may be shortened or dropped when many skills are installed. The folder is read-only to sandboxed commands, which is wanted.
simpler_alternative: Put the whole procedure in AGENTS.md (costs context on every turn and hits the 32 KiB cap).
reason: Mechanical equivalent with the same file format; keeps default reading short.
cheap_local_trial: Copy the skill into a scratch repo and check that codex debug prompt-input or the /skills list shows it.

candidate: agents/openai.yaml invocation policy for the skill
what: Optional file in a skill folder that sets interface metadata and can turn off implicit invocation.
problem_here: none found
mechanism: policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false would require the user to name the skill.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills (vendor docs, 2026-11-10).
maturity: Documented feature; first release not checked.
cost: One more product-specific file to maintain.
simpler_alternative: Leave the default, which allows implicit use.
reason: The kit wants the skill to load whenever training work starts, which is the default.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Marked instruction block in the root AGENTS.md
what: Codex concatenates AGENTS.md files from the project root down to the working directory into its instructions.
problem_here: Ports the kit's nine always-on rules to Codex.
mechanism: Installer merges one marked block into <repo>/AGENTS.md. Limits: 32 KiB combined by default (project_doc_max_bytes), one file per directory, and AGENTS.override.md shadows AGENTS.md in the same directory.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md (vendor docs, 2026-11-10). Not exercised.
maturity: Long-standing Codex feature; AGENTS.md is a cross-vendor convention.
cost: The installer must detect AGENTS.override.md and an existing file near the size cap. Whether the block survives compaction unchanged was not checked.
simpler_alternative: none found
reason: The standard instruction channel on Codex; mechanical and cheap.
cheap_local_trial: Add a block with a marker sentence to a scratch repo and inspect codex debug prompt-input.

candidate: project_doc_fallback_filenames to make Codex read CLAUDE.md
what: Config key listing extra file names Codex accepts when a directory has no AGENTS.md.
problem_here: Would let one instruction file serve two agents.
mechanism: project_doc_fallback_filenames = ['CLAUDE.md'] in user config or trusted project config.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/guides/agents-md (vendor docs, 2026-11-10).
maturity: Stable config key.
cost: Needs config that only loads for trusted projects or lives in the home directory; ignored as soon as an AGENTS.md exists in the directory; the existing block names paths of the current platform.
simpler_alternative: Write a second marked block into AGENTS.md.
reason: More fragile than writing AGENTS.md directly, and the two blocks need different paths anyway.
cheap_local_trial: none

candidate: Codex custom agents (.codex/agents/*.toml) for the reviewer and the analyst
what: Project-scoped agent definitions with name, description, developer instructions and optional model settings, started by the main agent on request.
problem_here: Ports the kit's two reviewer roles: an independent sceptical review and cheap log reading outside the main context.
mechanism: Two TOML files under <repo>/.codex/agents; the skill tells the main agent when to delegate.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/subagents (vendor docs, 2026-11-10): subagents inherit the parent's sandbox and approval settings, and instructions do not create a read-only sandbox. Not exercised.
maturity: Subagents are on by default in stable 0.167.0; first release not checked.
cost: Read-only is advice only; a reviewer inherits write access from its parent. Extra tokens per delegation. Needs a trusted project to load.
simpler_alternative: Ask the main agent to review its own work (the kit's evidence says agents grade themselves too kindly).
reason: Closest equivalent of the existing roles; documentation must state that read-only is not enforced unless one of the two enforcement options is added.
cheap_local_trial: Add one agent file to a scratch repo and ask Codex to delegate a file summary to it; watch the collab_tool_call items in --json output.

candidate: Read-only reviewers enforced by the PreToolUse hook using agent_type
what: The hook payload carries optional agent_id and agent_type fields for tool calls made by a subagent; the guard denies edits and mutating commands when the type is a reviewer role.
problem_here: Makes the reviewer roles mechanically read-only on Codex, as the kit does today with a dedicated hook.
mechanism: Guard rule: if agent_type is one of the kit's reviewer names, deny apply_patch and any command not on a read-only list.
evidence: Fields present in https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.167.0/codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/pre-tool-use.command.input.schema.json (read verbatim 2026-11-11). The value used for a custom agent and whether it is set on every call were not confirmed.
maturity: Schema of stable 0.167.0; fields are optional and not described in the vendor docs.
cost: Depends on an undocumented value; fail-open like every hook; a read-only command list for shell is hard to make complete.
simpler_alternative: Run the reviewer as a separate read-only codex exec process.
reason: Cheap if the field behaves as the schema suggests; must be confirmed in a live session first.
cheap_local_trial: Hook that appends the received payload to a file; spawn a custom agent that runs one command and inspect agent_type.

candidate: Reviewer as a separate process: codex exec --sandbox read-only --ephemeral
what: The harness, not the agent, starts a fresh read-only Codex run that reviews saved artifacts and returns a verdict.
problem_here: Gives an OS-enforced read-only reviewer with an independent context, which a subagent cannot provide on Codex.
mechanism: Harness calls codex exec with the read-only sandbox, a review prompt and -o to capture the verdict; --ephemeral avoids storing a session.
evidence: Read-only is the exec default, https://developers.openai.com/codex/noninteractive (2026-11-10); flags in local help of 0.167.0-alpha.3.2. Not exercised.
maturity: Stable flags in Codex CLI 0.167.0.

candidate: codex exec --json event stream for supervision and token accounting
what: JSON Lines on stdout with thread, turn and item events; turn.completed carries token usage.
problem_here: Lets harness code meter agent tokens against the user's limit and see commands, file changes and failures without parsing prose.
mechanism: Read stdout line by line; usage fields are input_tokens, cached_input_tokens, cache_write_input_tokens, output_tokens and reasoning_output_tokens; errors arrive as error and turn.failed events; exit status is 0 or 1.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/noninteractive (sample, 2026-11-10); https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.167.0/codex-rs/exec/src/exec_events.rs and event_processor_with_jsonl_output.rs in the same folder (read 2026-11-11). Not exercised.
maturity: Stable flag in Codex CLI 0.167.0; first release not checked.
cost: Usage is the thread total, not a per-turn figure, so the meter must subtract. Hook runs are absent from the stream. Usage caps and rate limits are only recognisable by message text. Money cost must be derived from tokens by the harness.
simpler_alternative: Count runs and wall-clock time only.
reason: Only machine-readable source of token usage in headless mode; needed for the user-set token limit.
cheap_local_trial: codex exec --json with a one-line prompt in a scratch repo; save the stream and check the fields, then resume the session and see whether usage grows cumulatively.

candidate: External budget supervisor around codex exec (time, runs, tokens)
what: Harness code owns the limits: it starts each agent run, watches the event stream and stops or refuses the next run when a limit is reached.
problem_here: codex exec has no flag for a turn, time or token cap, and its exit status does not distinguish a usage cap from other failures.
mechanism: Parent process with a deadline, a token meter fed by the JSON stream and a kill of the process tree on overrun; state saved between iterations.
evidence: Absence of cap flags in local codex exec --help (0.167.0-alpha.3.2, 2026-11-10); exit paths read in https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.167.0/codex-rs/exec/src/lib.rs (2026-11-11). A config key goals.max_goal_token_budget exists but its behaviour in exec was not checked.
maturity: Practice; standard-library code.
cost: Process-tree termination differs on Windows (no POSIX process groups); a killed run must leave resumable state; token totals must be subtracted correctly across resumes.
simpler_alternative: Trust the agent to stop when told in the prompt.
reason: Required by the brief (limits the agent cannot influence) and not provided by the platform.
cheap_local_trial: Wrap a trivial codex exec call in a script with a 30-second deadline and a long-running prompt; confirm the child tree is gone after the deadline on Windows and in WSL2.

candidate: One fresh codex exec run per loop iteration
what: The unattended loop is a harness loop; each iteration is a new headless agent run with a bounded task, instead of one long session.
problem_here: Keeps control, budget checks and keep-or-discard decisions in harness code between iterations, and avoids unbounded context growth.
mechanism: Harness writes the iteration brief, runs codex exec, evaluates with the frozen evaluator outside the agent, records the result, repeats.
evidence: A third-party Codex auto-research skill uses a detached controller that runs one codex exec worker per iteration in its background mode, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/leo-lilinxiao/codex-autoresearch/main/README.md (2026-11-11, author's description, no measurement).
maturity: Pattern in use by at least one project with about 3.2k stars; no comparative evidence found.

simpler_alternative: A single long session with a persistent goal.
reason: Matches the brief's requirement that harness code decides what is kept; needs a measured comparison of token cost against a single session.
cheap_local_trial: Two-iteration dry loop in a scratch repo with a fake evaluator and a tiny prompt; compare total tokens with one session doing both steps.

candidate: Minimum Codex version and version preflight
what: The Codex adapter checks codex --version and refuses or warns below a floor; documentation names the version it was tested against.
problem_here: Flags and hook behaviour change weekly (four stable releases between 23 Oct and 6 Nov 2026), and sandbox escapes were fixed during 2026.
mechanism: Parse codex --version; floor at the release that fixed the last known sandbox escape (0.149.0 per a third-party security note) or higher; tested-against version recorded in the install report.
evidence: Release dates from the vendor repository (2026-11-10); removal of --full-auto in https://developers.openai.com/codex/noninteractive (2026-11-10); escape fixed in CLI 0.149.0 per https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-openai-codex-sandbox-escapes-20260922-csa/ (third-party note, 2026-11-11). Vendor advisory pages were not reachable.
maturity: Practice.
cost: Floor needs maintenance; alpha builds such as the local 0.167.0-alpha.3.2 need a tolerant parser.
simpler_alternative: State the tested version in the README only.
reason: Cheap protection against silent behaviour changes in a fast-moving dependency.
cheap_local_trial: Run codex --version on both local builds (0.130.0-alpha.5 and 0.167.0-alpha.3.2) and feed the strings to the parser.

candidate: Isolated container or VM for full-access unattended runs
what: Run Codex with danger-full-access only inside a disposable container or VM that holds the repository and the GPU and nothing else of value.
problem_here: The one case in which the brief allows approvals to be bypassed; also the vendor's advice for containers, where the inner sandbox may not work.
mechanism: User-provided container with GPU passthrough; the kit documents the mode and checks an explicit marker before accepting full access.
evidence: https://developers.openai.com/codex/agent-approvals-security (2026-11-10) advises danger-full-access inside a container; a third-party security note advises a disposable VM or container for untrusted content, https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-openai-codex-sandbox-escapes-20260922-csa/ (2026-11-11).
maturity: Common practice; no kit-specific evidence.
cost: Needs a container runtime with GPU passthrough (on Windows that means WSL2), credentials must be kept out of the container, and the kit cannot verify isolation, only a declared marker.
simpler_alternative: workspace-write with a launcher allow rule on the host.
reason: Required by the brief as the only allowed bypass setting; off by default because it needs extra software.
cheap_local_trial: In WSL2, only if a GPU-enabled container runtime is already installed: run nvidia-smi inside a container; otherwise none.

candidate: Codex layout: kit files under .codex and .agents, run state under runs
what: Place guard, rules, config and skill in the two folders Codex makes read-only for sandboxed commands, and keep everything the agent's commands must write elsewhere.
problem_here: Gives a tamper-resistant kit for free in workspace-write mode, and avoids write failures for run state and journal.
mechanism: .codex/hooks.json, .codex/hooks/, .codex/rules/, .codex/agents/, the harness config under .codex/, the skill under .agents/skills/; runs and journal stay where they are; the guard log is written only by the hook process.
evidence: Protected paths quoted from https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-approvals-security (2026-11-11): .git, .agents, .codex and .aws are read-only recursively inside writable roots. The current kit keeps run state under runs by default (local file search, 2026-11-11). That hook processes run outside the sandbox is inferred from the runner source.
maturity: Practice built on documented behaviour.
cost: Two config locations when the same repository also uses the other agents; installer and controller need a platform-aware path lookup; protection holds only for sandboxed commands.
simpler_alternative: Reuse the existing kit paths on Codex (they would be writable by the agent).
reason: Free OS-level protection of the evaluator configuration and guard on Codex.
cheap_local_trial: In a scratch repo run codex sandbox with a command that writes one file under .codex and one under runs; expect the first to fail and the second to succeed.

candidate: Windows hook launch form: commandWindows without quotes or spaces
what: Give each hook a separate Windows command line that needs no quoting, or a small wrapper script at a path without spaces.
problem_here: On native Windows, hook commands with quoted paths are reported to never run, sometimes while Codex shows the hook as completed; python3 is usually absent.
mechanism: commandWindows set to a bare interpreter name and a repository-relative script path, or to a wrapper .cmd file; the installer refuses or warns when the repository path contains spaces.
evidence: commandWindows documented at https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks (2026-11-10); cmd /C outer-quote wrapping read in https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.167.0/codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/command_runner.rs (2026-11-11); failures reported in https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/38168, https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/57050 and https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49716 (user reports, all open, no maintainer reply).
maturity: Workaround for open upstream issues; may become unnecessary.
cost: Which shell runs the hook on a given machine is not documented; hooks run with the session working directory, so relative paths break if the session starts in a subfolder.
simpler_alternative: Support only WSL2 on Windows.
reason: Native Windows is first-class in the brief, and this is the most likely silent failure there.
cheap_local_trial: Scratch repo on native Windows with a hook that writes a marker file, tried in three forms (quoted path, unquoted path, wrapper script) from the repository root and from a subfolder.

candidate: PowerShell-aware command analysis in the guard
what: Teach the guard to recognise the protected actions when the command line is PowerShell rather than POSIX shell.
problem_here: On native Windows Codex appears to run commands through PowerShell while reporting the tool as Bash, so a POSIX tokenizer can miss a sealed-path read or a process kill.
mechanism: Detect the dialect from the platform and the command text; conservative substring and path checks for sealed and frozen paths in any dialect; deny when unsure.
evidence: PowerShell as the Windows session shell is stated in a user issue with source references, https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/49716, and the policy engine parses PowerShell command scripts (exec_policy.rs, paraphrased read, 2026-11-11); user reports say the hook payload omits the shell and the working directory, https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/44836 and https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/57184 (both open). Not confirmed in a session.
maturity: No existing implementation in the kit.
cost: A second shell grammar to approximate; false denials when conservative.
simpler_alternative: Declare native Windows partly advisory and recommend WSL2 for enforced runs.
reason: Needed for honest protection claims on native Windows, but the size of the gap must be measured first.
cheap_local_trial: Log three hook payloads from a native Windows session (file read, process stop, file delete) and run the current guard on them offline.

candidate: hooks.json rather than [hooks] tables in config.toml
what: Codex accepts hook declarations either as .codex/hooks.json or as TOML tables in .codex/config.toml.
problem_here: The stdlib-only installer can merge JSON safely on Python 3.8; it cannot write TOML with the standard library.
mechanism: Installer merges its entries into <repo>/.codex/hooks.json and leaves config.toml alone unless an optional feature needs it.
evidence: Both forms documented at https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks (2026-11-10); when one layer has both, Codex adds a warning that asks for a single representation per layer (discovery source, re-read verbatim 2026-11-11). Python's tomllib exists from 3.11 and only reads; the kit's README states Python 3.8+.
maturity: Documented, stable form.
cost: If the user already keeps hooks in config.toml, Codex prints a warning about two representations; MCP servers, permission profiles and custom agents still need TOML output.
simpler_alternative: n/a
reason: Keeps the core install dependency-free and the merge reversible.
cheap_local_trial: Unit test of the JSON merge and its backup; no Codex needed.
